item.title: Forum of Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT): 2026 Convention ‘One Industry, Many Voices: We Build Together’
item.description: The Forum of Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) will host its upcoming national convention on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos. Running from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM, the event centers on the theme “ One Industry, Many Voices: We Build Together. “ The gathering will unite women across film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and create agency for one another across sectors. Art cultural expert and curator Mrs. Sandra Mbanefo Obiago will deliver the keynote address. The program features interactive panel discussions, break-out sessions, speed networking, and a fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” Featured speakers and panellists joining the conversation include media executive Kadaria Ahmed, filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and Esosa Osagiede. item.title: Yemi Alade Is Counting Cash and Serving Looks in “Alhaja” Video
item.description: Yemi Alade wears a gold-embroidered black abaya in her “Alhaja” music video. We love how Yemi Alade gives us something new to talk about with each music video. If she isn’t channelling a photographer who could give Don Jazzy a run for his money, she’s stepping into the shoes of an Alhaja who clearly has money to spend, and she’s having a great time doing it. In the official music video for “Alhaja”, a standout track from her latest album, It’s Yemi Alade , the Afropop star leans into rich cultural aesthetics, striking outfits and scenes that feel like a celebration of success. Directed by Clarence Peters , the video plays with neon lighting, atmospheric torchlight and a cast that knows how to make an entrance. Yemi Alade holds a stack of cash in a scene from her “Alhaja” music video. Yemi has a wardrobe change for every mood, too. In one scene, she appears in a traditional red outfit, complete with a structured headwrap and layers of coral beads. Then comes a black-and-gold embroidered abaya, paired with bold gold hand jewellery and ornate rings. She’s giving us an Alhaja who knows exactly what she’s worth, and the styling makes sure we don’t miss it. Yemi Alade holds a stack of cash in a scene from her “Alhaja” music video. The details around her are just as fun. Vintage cars set the scene, traditional drums bring in the cultural touches, and cast members count cash beneath warm lanterns. It all adds to the video’s celebration of identity, prosperity and personal achievement, with Yemi right at the centre of it. With “Alhaja”, Yemi Alade gives us another music video with a distinct visual world, memorable styling and plenty of personality. And really, would we expect anything less? item.title: What is The Hidden Cost of Nigerian Women’s Unpaid Labour?
item.description: Mother and children preparing food in a bright, cosy kitchen setting. Credit: RDNE Stock Project/Pexels. Fadekemi was six when she first felt the sting of splattered hot oil on her skin. She recalls her mother’s stern voice instructing her on how to make stew the way her father liked it. Fifty-one years and thousands of stew pots later, Fadekemi still wonders if that’s all she was made to do. In different parts of Nigeria today, there are millions of women like Fadekemi, each spending at least 5 hours daily on unpaid care and domestic work. Although Nigerians rarely pay women for care and domestic duties, research shows that it is real work with an annual economic value of up to $111 billion . How Women Carry Nigeria’s Unpaid Labour According to the Nigeria Time Use Survey (NTUS) 2024 report, the average Nigerian woman spends 21% of her day on unpaid domestic and care work ; this equals 5 extra hours, while men spend just one hour on unpaid work. This means that after spending 8 hours at work, she spends another 5 hours doing childcare and household work, making it a double shift. Yet when you look at the economic drivers of Nigeria’s economy, her time or work does not count; it is seen as a woman’s work. This inequality is seen as invisible labour. We see it show up in different phases of women’s lives, yet we still miss how heavy an unequal burden this is. Right from when a girl is 13, she becomes an unpaid labourer, doing domestic chores, taking care of siblings, yet these contributions are seen as nothing to Nigeria’s GDP. For Fadekemi, this unpaid labour started at six, continued into her teenage years, where she became a caregiver for her siblings, extended into motherhood, and now, as a grandmother, she continues to be a caregiver for her grandchildren because even traditions like Omugwo exclude men from care duties. Behind those hours of unpaid labour is a missed opportunity for the country’s GDP growth. What Happens When Care Is Shared? In a 2026 study published in BMC Paediatrics, over 64% of women said they were the primary caregivers of their newborn children. In some cases, this is a result of traditional belief systems that reinforce gender roles and assign domestic duties to women. In other cases, it is a systemic failure caused by policies that reinforce gender inequality. In Nigeria, for example, mothers are entitled to maternity leave with 50% pay, while only fathers in the civil service are entitled to 14 days of paternity leave. So what happens to private sector fathers? The national policy designs them to be absent fathers from day one and reinforces the narrative that their sole role is to be a provider and presence doesn’t matter. Experts have highlighted that cutting a new mother’s salary by 50% while excluding most fathers from paid leave reinforces the belief that a man’s primary duty is to be a financial provider and makes it harder for them to be present. And when that happens, care once again becomes the woman’s job.

item.title: 25 and Golden! Dede Ashiogwu Celebrates in a Gorgeous Butter-Yellow Two-Piece
item.description: Dede celebrates her 25th birthday in a draped butter yellow chiffon set. Butter yellow on melanin is already a winning combination, but Big Brother Naija Season 10 star Dede is taking it somewhere much more fabulous. Celebrating her birthday on 23 October 2026, the content creator, whose full name is Ashiogwu Precious , has gifted us a set of Renaissance-inspired portraits that could easily pass for paintings in a grand old gallery. And the outfit at the centre of it all? A custom butter-yellow two-piece that makes a very good case for giving this pretty shade a spot in your wardrobe. Dede wears a custom butter yellow gathering bandeau top and low-rise train skirt by Precious Phillips. Dede handled the creative direction herself, working with designer Precious Phillips on a gathered bandeau top and a low-rise maxi skirt that follows her figure before spilling into a floor-sweeping train. The colour is gorgeous against her skin, and that dramatic silhouette gives the look a regal, almost otherworldly quality without feeling stuck in another century. Of course, the beauty look had to keep up. Yellow feathers frame her eyes, a thick side-braided ponytail sweeps through her hair, and her glowing makeup ties everything together. Add a golden hand mirror and a moody, canvas-style backdrop, and you have birthday portraits that look as though they were dreamed up in an artist’s studio. Dede poses with a golden handheld mirror in her self-styled Renaissance birthday shoot. The best part is that you don’t need a Renaissance-inspired photoshoot to take a little inspiration from Dede. Butter yellow works beautifully in flowing chiffon, sheer mesh and other lightweight fabrics, whether you’re dressing for a birthday dinner or simply want to try something new. Gold jewellery complements the shade beautifully, while pared-back accessories give statement silhouettes and playful eye makeup room to shine. Dede complements her birthday look with soft yellow feather eye flourishes and gold leaf drop earrings. Dede may have given butter yellow the full birthday-treatment treatment, but the takeaway is simple: this shade deserves a place in your fashion rotation. Ashiogwu Precious (Dede) marks her 25th birthday in a butter yellow two-piece set by Precious Phillips. item.title: Janelle Monáe Spreads Her Fashion Wings in a Sculptural Robert Wun Gown
item.description: Janelle Monáe wears a custom blue sequined Robert Wun gown at the 2026 Academy Museum Gala. Butterfly in a dress? Janelle Monáe says bring it on! We’ve seen butterflies inspire jewellery, hair accessories and even prints on dresses, but a giant, three-dimensional butterfly forming the bodice of a gown? Now that’s something worth talking about. And who better to wear it than the acclaimed singer, songwriter, and actress Janelle Monáe, who has never been afraid to have a little fun with fashion? For the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala, held on 17 October 2026 in Los Angeles, the singer and actress known for her memorable roles in Hidden Figures , Moonlight , and Glass Onion , stepped onto the red carpet in a Robert Wun creation that looked like a butterfly had spread its wings right across her chest. The gown, from the designer’s Fall 2026 Couture collection, featured a fitted mermaid silhouette covered in sequins that moved from rich blue to black. But the real attraction was that enormous three-dimensional butterfly bodice, with its wings extending across her upper body. Janelle Monáe attends the 2026 Academy Museum Gala in a custom Robert Wun mermaid dress. And Janelle wasn’t about to let the butterfly theme end with the dress. Styled by Alexandra Mandelkorn , she paired the gown with sheer opera-length gloves, metallic blue stiletto nails and a soft pixie cut finished with a little butterfly hair clip. Even the smallest details played along with the look, without competing with that spectacular bodice. Janelle Monáe in custom Robert Wun Couture at the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala. Now, if you’re wondering how to borrow a little inspiration from this look without wearing an enormous butterfly to your next event, there’s something to learn from Janelle’s styling. When your outfit already has a striking feature, you can afford to keep everything else simple. Skip the heavy necklaces, let the shape of the dress do its thing and choose accessories that complement its colours. And those shades of blue are worth experimenting with, too. Cobalt, navy and other rich jewel tones can look beautiful together, especially when you carry a little of the colour into your makeup or accessories. Janelle’s look might be straight from the couture runway, but the styling ideas are ones you can have fun with in your own wardrobe. Janelle Monáe showcases the three-dimensional butterfly bodice of her Robert Wun Fall 2026 Couture gown. And who better to wear it than the acclaimed singer, songwriter, and actress Janelle Monáe, who has never been afraid to have a little fun with fashion? For the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala, held on 17 October 2026 in Los Angeles, the singer and actress known for her memorable roles in Hidden Figures , Moonlight , and Glass Onion , stepped onto the red carpet in a Robert Wun creation that looked like a butterfly had spread its wings right across her chest. The gown, from the designer’s Fall 2026 Couture collection, featured a fitted mermaid silhouette covered in sequins that moved from rich blue to black. But the real attraction was that enormous three-dimensional butterfly bodice, with its wings extending across her upper body. Janelle Monáe attends the 2026 Academy Museum Gala in a custom Robert Wun mermaid dress. And Janelle wasn’t about to let the butterfly theme end with the dress. Styled by Alexandra Mandelkorn , she paired the gown with sheer opera-length gloves, metallic blue stiletto nails and a soft pixie cut finished with a little butterfly hair clip. Even the smallest details played along with the look, without competing with that spectacular bodice. Janelle Monáe in custom Robert Wun Couture at the 6th Annual Academy Museum Gala. Now, if you’re wondering how to borrow a little inspiration from this look without wearing an enormous butterfly to your next event, there’s something to learn from Janelle’s styling. When your outfit already has a striking feature, you can afford to keep everything else simple. Skip the heavy necklaces, let the shape of the dress do its thing and choose accessories that complement its colours. And those shades of blue are worth experimenting with, too. Cobalt, navy and other rich jewel tones can look beautiful together, especially when you carry a little of the colour into your makeup or accessories. Janelle’s look might be straight from the couture runway, but the styling ideas are ones you can have fun with in your own wardrobe. Janelle Monáe showcases the three-dimensional butterfly bodice of her Robert Wun Fall 2026 Couture gown. item.title: Adekunle Gold Foundation and PESA Launch ‘We Are Not Done’ Sickle Cell Impact Initiative
item.description: The Adekunle Gold Foundation (AG Foundation), in partnership with Pesa , has launched We’re Not Done: AG Foundation Sickle Cell Impact Initiative , a new programme designed to strengthen organisations providing critical support to people living with sickle cell disease. Launching with a $20,000 commitment from Pesa , the initiative will provide funding to selected sickle cell organisations, helping them expand their work across healthcare access, patient support, education, awareness and advocacy. For its inaugural cycle, We’re Not Done will support AG Foundation’s work alongside the following 4 beneficiaries, Sickle Cell Advocacy Management Initiative (NIGERIA), Not Just You (CANADA), Sickle Life (GHANA), It Takes A Village (UK) recognizing the important work each organisation is already doing within the sickle cell community. The funding will enable the organisations to strengthen existing programmes, expand their reach and deepen their impact. For A dekunle Gold, who has lived openly with sickle cell disease and used his platform to advocate for the community, We’re Not Done represents a commitment to supporting the organisations already doing vital work on the ground. “ We’re Not Done is about turning awareness into action. There are incredible organisations working every day to improve the lives of people living with sickle cell, and together with Pesa, we want to give them more resources to do that work and reach even more people.” Adekunle Gold said. Pesa joins the initiative as its programme partner , supporting both the launch and first cycle of impact. “ Sickle cell affects many people in the Nigerian and wider Black communities we serve. These are our friends, colleagues, and loved ones. Adekunle Gold has shown how a personal connection to an issue can become a force for meaningful change, and we’re proud to support the launch of We’re Not Done , an initiative dedicated to raising awareness and supporting the sickle cell community. Through our partnership with the AG Foundation and the other participating foundations, we hope to go beyond awareness and contribute to meaningful, tangible support for individuals and families affected by sickle cell, ” said Tosin Olaniyi (Head, Global Growth & Marketing, Pesa) Through We’re Not Done , AG Foundation, with the support of Pesa, aims to build a platform that combines funding, advocacy and visibility to strengthen the wider sickle cell ecosystem and create measurable, lasting impact. The foundation is committed to improving the lives of those living with sickle cell disease through healthcare access, advocacy, and awareness. item.title: Veteran Nollywood Actor Francis Duru Passes Away at 57 | Read Family Statement
item.description: Veteran Nollywood actor Francis Duru has passed away at the age of 57. Photo Credit: Francis Duru/Instagram The Nigerian film industry has been thrown into mourning following the sad passing of veteran Nollywood actor, director,and academic, Francis Duru . The respected movie star passed away at the age of 57 following a brief illness, leaving behind a incredible legacy that spans over three decades of memorable performances across television and cinema. Sharing the heartbreaking news with fans and well-wishers on his official Instagram page, his family released a moving statement: We, the family of Francis Duru, regret to announce his passing following a brief illness. We appreciate your prayers, love, and understanding. May his soul rest in perfect peace. Amen. A true pioneer of modern Nollywood, Francis Duru made his screen debut back in 1989 in the feature Missing Mark , before shooting to nationwide fame for his unforgettable portrayal of Ahanna in Amaka Igwe ’s 1995 classic Rattlesnake . Over the years, he cemented his status as a household name with stellar roles in acclaimed movies such as Blood Money , Mama Sunday , Total Control , Home in Exile , Mboputa , and Stigma . Beyond his stellar career in front of the camera, Duru was a dedicated academic holding a degree in Theatre Arts from the University of Port Harcourt, and a passionate advocate who served as a United Nations Ambassador of Peace and as interim President of the Actors Guild of Nigeria (AGN). item.title: Naomi Ackie Was Anything but Basic in Sculptural Schiaparelli at Paris Fashion Week
item.description: Naomi Ackie Naomi Ackie has been delivering some serious fashion moments lately, and her appearance at the Schiaparelli show during Paris Fashion Week is another one for the books. The British-Grenadian actress wore a striking black, single-sleeved gown that perfectly captured the house’s surrealist sensibility. Thousands of finely worked pleats created an almost liquid effect, hugging her figure before falling into a dramatic thigh-high slit. But what really makes this look special is the exaggerated sleeve, which gives the otherwise sleek silhouette an architectural quality. Naomi has worn the brand a few times, and we love how she always embraces the brand’s aesthetic without letting it overwhelm her. The sculptural statement earrings and signature face-motif clutch brought just the right amount of the house’s eccentricity, while her slicked-back ponytail kept the overall look sharp and modern. Through workshops, conferences, and industry engagements, she became increasingly exposed to the renewable energy sector at a time when Nigeria was slowly beginning to embrace alternative energy solutions. She later transitioned into a sales executive role before eventually building her own solar installation company. Established in 2013, Energy Excell Systems and Solutions Limited operates as an indigenous Nigerian renewable energy social enterprise and Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) company. But beyond simply installing solar panels, the company focused heavily on what Nkechi describes as “productive use” energy. The company provided homes, small businesses, and farming communities with energy-efficient appliances such as solar-powered rice mills, cassava graters, and grinders: tools capable of directly improving livelihoods and local economies. item.title: Cynthia Erivo’s Fashion Range Is Beyond Impeccable
item.description: @jasonbolden If there’s one thing Cynthia Erivo has mastered, it’s the art of keeping us guessing. Whether she’s embracing full-throttle red carpet glamour or experimenting with more directional silhouettes, the British actress rarely plays it safe. And judging by her latest appearances, she’s showing no signs of slowing down. For the Prima Facie premiere at the BFI London Film Festival, Cynthia delivered a welcome dose of sunshine in a custom canary-yellow Prada gown. The bias-cut satin skimmed her figure beautifully, falling into a sweeping train, while oversized black grosgrain bows at the shoulders added a graphic contrast to the otherwise minimalist silhouette. @jasonbolden And she’s just as convincing in something that’s more casual but still directional. Case in point: the tan leather Proenza Schouler Fall 2026 co-ord she wore in New York. With its structured double-breasted jacket, relaxed trousers and chunky platform shoes, the look could easily have felt overwhelming. Instead, Cynthia made a compelling case for exaggerated proportions, proving that a neutral palette doesn’t have to mean playing it safe. Her final appearance at New York Comic Con, where she joined the cast of Children of Blood and Bone in another Proenza Schouler Fall 2026 creation also designed by new Proenza Schouler Creative Director Rachel Scott (also of Diotima). This time, she opted for a navy printed dress featuring sculptural draping, an asymmetric silhouette and dramatic fringed detailing. The silver grommets along the hem introduced an unexpected industrial edge, while glittering blue heels and statement jewellery completed the look. item.title: Smirnoff Ice and BBNaija: A Season of Being Bolder with Ice
item.description: Three months, four pool parties, two Saturday night parties and one unforgettable task Smirnoff Ice has left its mark on the BBNaija house. The season was a full celebration of what Bolder with Ice stands for: self expression without limits. Inside the house, that meant housemates showing different sides of themselves depending on their mood, and the energy of the moment, and Smirnoff Ice was right there for every one of them. The pool parties set the tone early. With music playing and a cold Smirnoff Ice in hand, the housemates danced, had fun in the pool and laughed their way through every moment. Some stayed in the pool, others at the edge, while some didn’t stop dancing the whole time. That’s kind of the beauty of Bolder with Ice, there really isn’t a “ right ” way to experience it. You just show up, find your pace, and take it all in. Whether you’re there to lose yourself in the music or just relax with a cold drink, the whole point is simply being there and enjoying the moment. The Saturday night parties carried that same energy into the evening. The housemates stepped out in outfits they picked for themselves, danced to the music and enjoyed the night with their friends in the house. Every look and every dance move was theirs, which is exactly the kind of individuality the brand was built to celebrate. Then there was the Smirnoff Ice task: Bolder With Ice Challenge, where the house got to play, create and compete. Broken telephone, the Ice Throne styling challenge, the memory game, Shadow Partner and the painting round gave the housemates room to show their humour, their style, their focus and their creativity. Team Original and Team Double Black went head to head, but the real win was the laughter and the personality that came out of every round. That is what made the Smirnoff Ice season special. Across the pool parties, the Saturday night parties and the task, there was always room for every mood. The loud one, the quiet one, the stylish one, the playful one, the competitive one, all of them had a place and all of them had a good time. Smirnoff Ice did not ask the housemates to be anything other than themselves, and that is exactly the idea behind Bolder with Ice. As the season comes to an end, the memories will stay: the music, the pool, the dance floor, the games and the friendships built along the way. Thanks to every single housemate who brought their own kind of bold to the house, and a massive thank you to everyone who tuned in, laughed, and celebrated with us all season long. Until the next season, stay bold, stay chilled, and stay you. item.title: Broda Shaggi Reveals He Was Hit by a Stray Bullet in New Documentary
item.description: Samuel Animashaun Perry (Broda Shaggi) explains the stray bullet incident behind his months-long hiatus in a new video. If you are a fan of Broda Shaggi ‘s skits, his music, or even just his lively presence on your timelines, you must have noticed that the popular entertainer and actor has been noticeably absent from social media over the past few months. Samuel Animashaun Perry has now officially returned, bringing along a deeply moving mini-documentary that breaks his silence and reveals the terrifying life-threatening ordeal behind his sudden hiatus . The multi-AMVCA winner revealed that his unexpected break was caused by a horrific incident where he was struck by a stray bullet while returning from a shoot. Recounting the frightening moment, Broda Shaggi shared,”We were done shooting and were on our way when we got stuck in a holdup. Suddenly, I heard a loud bang and everywhere went silent. I could see people talking, but I couldn’t hear anything. Then I touched my hip and saw blood. That was when it dawned on me that I had been hit by a stray bullet.” Broda Shaggi in an eccentric futuristic costume for one of his signature video skits. The incident led to an emergency hospital admission, extensive medical procedures, and an intensive period of physical rehabilitation . For a performer whose entire craft relies on boundless physical energy, comedy, and stage presence, being bedridden and unable to move presented immense physical and emotional hurdles . In the video, he candidly reflects on the overwhelming fear of losing his mobility and the uncertainty of how he would continue doing what he loves . Tracing his road from severe setback to resurgence, the documentary shows his gradual process of learning to walk again, moving from complete immobility to crutches and eventually regaining his strength . Now stepping back in front of the camera on his own terms, Broda Shaggi is turning what could have been a tragic end into a triumphant second chapter, ready to reconnect with his fans and dive back into his creative work . item.title: Olamide Wants Us to Party on “Burukutu” | Watch Video
item.description: Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram When the YBNL Nation boss decides to drop new music, the entire continent pauses to listen. Olamide is back in his absolute element, and the music community is buzzing following a major surprise release that has everyone talking. Building on the momentum of his previous self-titled album Olamidé released last year, the rap icon has dropped a brand-new single while officially setting the timeline for his next massive project. Olamide’s latest single is titled “ Burukutu ”. Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage found across various parts of Nigeria, the track leans heavily into street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, opening with the infectious chant, “Baddoo we wanna partyyyy!” Lyrically, Olamide weaves sharp street-smart Yoruba flows with rhythmic cadences, reflecting on hustle, leisure, and local vibes over high-energy production. Olamide holding a saxophone on the courtyard set of his Burukutu music video. Photo Credit: Styling The Stars With Swazzi/Instagram The accompanying music video directed by TG Omori matches the song’s intense cultural weight visually. It cuts dynamically between a monochromatic, glowing red corridor—where Olamide appears sharply tailored in a double-breasted suit, dark sunglasses, and dreadlocks—and an earthen-toned, arched outdoor courtyard filled with rhythmic background dancers in structured white outfits, pillbox hats, and pearl details, alongside striking scenes of Olamide stepping up to play the saxophone. Alongside the release of “Burukutu,” Olamide surprised fans by announcing the official title of his forthcoming studio project: Time & Space. Marking another milestone in his legendary discography, Time & Space is officially scheduled to drop on November 16, 2026, proving yet again why the icon remains at the very heartbeat of African music. item.title: 3 Toyin Abraham-Inspired Owambe Looks for Your Next Saturday Party
item.description: Three traditional Owambe style moments from Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi featuring velvet, damask, and aso-oke. When Nollywood actor and filmmaker Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi is not busy preparing for her highly anticipated festive cinematic release, Bestie , or writing, producing, and starring in box-office hits like Fate of Alakada , Ijakumo : The Born Again Stripper , and The Ghost and the Tout , she is usually showing us how to nail weekend celebrations. As one of the most prominent faces in Nigerian cinema, her personal style outside the cinema hall has become a major source of fashion inspiration, especially when it comes to pulling off unforgettable Owambe looks. Styling traditional wear for a Saturday party comes down to knowing how to mix colours, textures, and rich fabrics without losing that classic touch. Wearing black and silver to a Nigerian party is all about balance. While dark tones are traditionally avoided for daytime celebrations, pairing a deep black velvet blouse with a metallic silver scalloped-lace skirt completely changes the mood. Draping a silver-grey paisley ipele over the shoulder alongside a matching pleated geleadds instant brightness, while traditional coral beads anchor the entire outfit. Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi showing how to wear black and silver to a Nigerian party. Photo Credit: Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi/Instagram For anyone leaning towards rich jewel tones, crimson velvet offers an instant sense of luxury. Tailoring a solid burgundy velvet gown into a clean, floor-length silhouette provides a sleek base, but adding a patterned teal and magenta damask ipele across one shoulder breaks up the solid fabric. Crowning the look with a structured fan gele in the same damask print brings the entire outfit together. Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi styling crimson velvet and patterned damask for traditional Owambe inspiration. Photo Credit: Toyin Abraham Ajeyemi/Instagram Bright colours always command attention in party halls, and mustard yellow offers a warmer, sophisticated take on sunshine yellow. Tailoring the fabric into a traditional buba and iro set with horizontal black lace bands and tassel-fringe details along the wrapper adds movement and texture. Matching the ensemble with a rounded mustard gele and subtle gold jewellery keeps the palette grounded while letting the traditional silhouette shine. One day, he started paying closer attention to the tiny creatures around him and was amazed by what he was seeing. There were colours, patterns, behaviours and details that he had never noticed before. It felt like discovering an entirely different world that had been right in front of me all along. Dara self-taught himself macro photography, and the seemingly small curiosity during the pandemic has grown into a journey of documenting biodiversity across Nigeria, Canada, Costa Rica, Mexico, Ecuador and beyond. In the rainforests of Costa Rica and Ecuador, I’ve encountered creatures with some of the most remarkable adaptations I’ve ever seen. In Canada, I’ve spent countless hours photographing tiny wildlife in places people walk past every day. Even a small garden can be home to an incredible diversity of species. But returning to photograph in Nigeria was particularly meaningful to me. Treehopper by Nigerian macro photographer, Dara Ojo. Nigeria has an extraordinary range of habitats, from tropical rainforests in the south to savannas in the north, supporting an incredible variety of life. When people think about African wildlife, the conversation often centres on lions, elephants and other large animals. But there’s an entire world of smaller creatures that rarely receive the same attention. During my time photographing in Nigeria, I encountered some fascinating species, including the praying mantis that eventually became the cover of my book. After travelling across different continents and photographing so many remarkable creatures, the photograph chosen to represent my first book came from Nigeria. Mantis, by Nigerian macro photographer Dara Ojo. Let’s talk about the book Yes! Tiny Titans: The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem . My first photography book. Tell us about it and what you hope people take away from the book? This book means a great deal to me because it represents six years of curiosity, exploration and learning. It brings together around 120 of my photographs from different parts of the world, alongside stories about the creatures I’ve encountered and the important roles they play in nature. I wanted to create something that people could enjoy visually, but that would also encourage them to think differently about creatures they might normally overlook. They pollinate plants, recycle nutrients, help control populations of other organisms and provide food for countless species. Without them, the ecosystems we depend on would look very different. It follows my journey through different countries, including Nigeria, where I grew up, and Canada, where I now live. I’m also incredibly honoured that Dr John Acorn , a respected Canadian entomologist and science communicator, wrote the foreword. I hope someone picks up the book because they find the photographs interesting, but finishes it with a greater appreciation for the natural world, so that the next time they encounter a spider in their house or an unfamiliar insect in their garden, instead of immediately reaching for something to kill it, they’ll stop for a moment and take a closer look. _ Dara Ojo’s Tiny Titans: The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem will be published on November 10, 2026, and will be available internationally. item.title: How to Protect Yourself From Ebola Virus Disease
item.description: PPE Preparation in an Ebola Clinic. Generated Image. Yesterday, October 20, 2026, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) announced the confirmation of the first Ebola virus disease case in Abuja. While the federal government and the NCDC have continued strengthening surveillance and response efforts to prevent its spread, it is important for Nigerian citizens to also stay alert, safe and take preventive measures. According to the NCDC , “Ebola virus disease (EVD), also known as Ebola hemorrhagic fever (EHF), is a severe disease of humans and other primates caused by an RNA virus of the family Filoviridae and genus Ebola virus. The disease has a high fatality rate, killing between 25%-90% of those infected. Research conducted in 2005 suggested fruit bats to be the likely reservoir due to their ability to spread the virus without being affected by it. The largest outbreak to date took place in West Africa between March 2014 and June 2016, affecting Guinea, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Nigeria primarily. A total of 11,296 cases were recorded, including suspected and probable cases.” The first-ever case of Ebola in Nigeria was confirmed in Lagos on 23 July 2014, and with its high fatality rate, citizens need to understand how to protect themselves before the government’s intervention. According to the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Affairs , here are how you can protect yourself from Ebola virus disease: Advice to Nigerians Nigerians are advised to: Practice good hand hygiene. Wash your hands regularly with soap under running water or use hand sanitisers when soap and water are not readily available. Avoid physical contact with anyone who has symptoms of an infection with an unknown diagnosis. Reduce the risk of wildlife-to-human transmission from contact with infected fruit bats or monkeys/apes and the consumption of raw meat. Animals should be handled with gloves and other appropriate protective clothing. Animal products should be thoroughly cooked before consumption. Avoid direct contact with the blood, saliva, vomit, urine and other bodily fluids of suspected or confirmed EVD cases. If you or someone you know (with a travel history to any country with Ebola cases) experiences symptoms of EVD enumerated above, call 6232 or your State Ministry of Health hotline IMMEDIATELY for guidance. Advice to Healthcare Workers Healthcare workers: Are advised to maintain a high index of suspicion for EVD in their encounter with their patients Ensure strict isolation of the patient(s). Adhere strictly to infection prevention and control (IPC) measures, including the use of appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) like face masks, hand gloves, appropriate gowns, safe sharps disposal and others. Report suspected cases immediately to the NCDC or State Ministry of Health for appropriate response and management. Advice to Travellers Travellers are advised to: Shelter-in-place to avoid further spread through shared transport

item.title: From Sequins to Cow Print, See the Rave Glam Looks at the Tele x Zikora Premiere
item.description: Sophia Chisom, Mike Afolarin, and Genoveva Umeh interpreting the rave glam dress code for Tele x Zikora. A Nollywood premiere is always a good excuse to dress up, but when the dress code says “rave glam,” you know the red carpet is going to be anything but ordinary. That was the scene at the premiere of Tele x Zikora , where the cast and guests stepped out in bold colours, unexpected combinations and outfits that gave us plenty to look at. Written, produced and directed by Adenike Adebayo – Esho , Tele x Zikora is a campus romance set at the fictional Lagos Metropolitan University. The film follows two young people from very different worlds whose paths cross, setting the stage for a love story. Ahead of its cinema release on 23 October 2026, the cast and crew gathered to celebrate, with the evening’s rave glam theme giving everyone room to experiment with their style. Tele x Zikora writer, producer, and director Adenike Adebayo-Esho at the film premiere. Photo Credit: Adenike Adebayo-Esho/Instagram Sophia Chisom gave us a colour combination we wouldn’t have immediately put together, and somehow, it worked. She wore a royal blue longline coat over a matching top with a sharp white collar and cuffs, pairing both with a burnt-orange wrap mini skirt. An orange beret, star drop earrings and white knee-high boots completed her look. Mike Afolarin took a different route with a cow-print shearling jacket, a black top and dark grey flared jeans featuring silver side-buckle details. He finished with a dark cap, keeping things casual while still having a little fun with the dress code. Mike Afolarin at the Tele x Zikora premiere in a cow-print jacket and flare jeans. Photo Credit: Mike Afolarin/Instagram Then there was Genoveva Umeh in magenta and rose-pink sequins. Her dress featured structured shoulders and an asymmetrical skirt with long, shredded ribbons that moved as she walked. She paired it with deep pink tights and metallic heels, making a strong case for wearing pink from head to toe. And those were only a few of the looks from the night. item.title: Meet Solange Omon, the 21-Year-Old Cameroonian Model Who Made Her Victoria’s Secret Runway Debut
item.description: Solange Omon walking the runway in illuminated wings and a sweeping metallic train at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram Did you see an African woman on the runway of the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show? She walked with such a composed, smooth step that you couldn’t help but notice her as she stepped out into the bright spotlights of Los Angeles. Her name is Solange Omon , a 21-year-old rising star who has officially earned her wings as the newest Victoria’s Secret Angel. She secured her place on the global stage after beating over 100,000 applicants in the brand’s open casting search, Angels Among Us. The competition, documented in a special YouTube series, crowned her as the winner, awarding her a one-year modelling contract with IMG Models alongside her runway debut. Solange Omon with fellow Angels Among Us top 3 finalists Andreína Martínez and Tatyana Tinsley. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram Born in Cameroon as the eldest of six children, Solange moved to the United States and has spent the last few years living in Lewiston, Maine. Before entering the national spotlight, her everyday life looked quite different. She spent her time balancing university coursework with her job as a programme coordinator for a local non-profit organisation focused on supporting young people. Her work centred on helping Black and immigrant teenagers apply for jobs, find professional mentors, and access higher education resources across her community. When she attended the open casting call in Chicago, she carried that grounded background straight onto the runway. For her big moment, she wore a contrast ivory and black lace lingerie set featuring a plunge bra paired with high-cut briefs, styled with oversized gold hoop drop earrings . The focus of her outfit was a pair of illuminated golden wings featuring embedded warm lights, paired with a sweeping bronze metallic train attached at the base of the wings . Solange Omon walking the runway in illuminated wings and a sweeping metallic train at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Solange Omon/Instagram As she walked down the glossy black runway, she held the edges of her metallic train, letting the lightweight fabric float behind her as she moved . Midway through her walk, she turned toward the cameras with a warm smile, twirled gracefully on the catwalk, and gestured to the audience before stepping back up the stage . Her milestone victory marks a significant moment for African representation in global fashion, showing how a young woman from Central Africa went from community work to one of the most recognised runways in the world. Solange Omon backstage at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show in Los Angeles after earning her Angel wings. item.description: Folorunso Alakija with Vice-Chancellor Professor David Cole at the University of Buckingham. Now, the University of Buckingham in the United Kingdom has recognised her achievements with an honorary doctorate, celebrating her contributions to business, philanthropy and society. The honour was conferred on Friday, 16 October 2026, at the university’s Radcliffe Centre during Buckingham Africa Day, as the institution marked its 50th anniversary. Dressed in a red doctoral gown, Alakija received the degree from Vice-Chancellor Professor David Cole , with family, friends and members of the university community in attendance. For Alakija, the occasion was also an opportunity to speak to the next generation about ambition, responsibility and the importance of creating opportunities for others. Folorunso Alakija in her doctoral gown at the University of Buckingham conferment ceremony. Accepting the honorary degree, she thanked God and the university for the recognition, sharing her belief in Africa’s potential and the responsibility that comes with achievement. “Africa is a continent of immense potential, creativity and resilience and that achievement carries responsibility to serve others,” she said. She also encouraged students and young people to pursue their goals with passion, perseverance and diligence, while remaining humble and recognising the value of their contributions. Her message reflects a career that has taken her through several fields. Before becoming widely known for her work in oil and gas through Famfa Oil, Alakija worked in banking and established herself in Nigeria’s fashion industry. She has also been involved in real estate, printing and philanthropic initiatives supporting education, women and vulnerable communities. African wellness is evolving, and BEYOND Fitness Africa is helping shape what comes next. Built around the theme Rest, Reset and Recover , the three-day experience invites guests to step away from everyday demands and reconnect with their wellbeing through movement, personalised recovery, nourishing food, meaningful connections and genuine rest. What began as a boutique fitness studio in Victoria Island has evolved into a wellness business spanning corporate wellness, destination retreats and brand collaborations, with ambitions to expand beyond Lagos into other Nigerian and African markets. Sometimes it’s movement and the energy of a community. Other times, it’s rest, recovery or simply the freedom to do nothing. “As we look towards expanding BEYOND beyond Lagos, our ambition is to build a distinctly African wellness brand that delivers exceptional experiences while helping people live healthier, fuller lives.” Three Days of Movement, Recovery and Connection BEYOND on Tour V offers an all-inclusive retreat where guests can shape their weekend around what they need most. The experience includes personalised IV infusions, full-body massages, assisted stretching, breathwork, recovery treatments and specialist wellness consultations, alongside thoughtfully curated dining and entertainment. Movement enthusiasts can enjoy Sunrise Sculpt, Aqua Conditioning, golf, mobility and Total Body Strength with adidas OG Sport. Aquafina, the Official Hydration Partner, supports guests throughout the programme. Beyond physical wellbeing, Mrs Ifeoma Monye will lead Pretty Balancing Act: Creating a Life System That Works , an insightful conversation on creating practical systems that support personal wellbeing, professional ambitions and the demands of everyday life. A highlight of the weekend is the return of the signature Sunset Ride, featuring a live performance by Loud Urban Choir beside the lake. Guests can also enjoy the performance from La Roche-Posay’s Sunset Viewing Lounge. The evening continues with Filmhouse After Dark, featuring karaoke, barbecue and cinema under the stars. BYD joins as Official Mobility Partner, while Instax, the Official Memory Partner, captures moments from the weekend. Together, these experiences bring BEYOND’s approach to movement, restoration and community to life. The brand will also present Sunrise Sculpt, integrating skin health awareness into outdoor movement. For Williams, the collaboration reflects the importance of looking at wellbeing more holistically. “Wellbeing goes beyond exercise. It’s about understanding how different aspects of our health work together. Our partnership with La Roche-Posay brings skin health into that conversation, giving guests access to specialist knowledge they can apply in their everyday lives.” Beyond the Retreat: La Roche-Posay Living Lab Opens in Lagos Just days after BEYOND on Tour V, La Roche-Posay will bring its Living Lab to Victoria Island, Lagos, on 5 and 6 November 2026. The immersive public experience will bring together scientists, dermatologists, patients and consumers to explore skincare innovation and encourage meaningful conversations around skin health. Visitors will journey through five interactive stages: Discover, Test, Experience, Learn and Consult. The experience will feature Innovation Corners dedicated to La Roche-Posay’s Effaclar, Anthelios, Mela B3, Cicaplast and Lipikar ranges, alongside the LRP Café, expert discussions, the Scars of Life Cinema and professional skincare consultations. The event will take place at Plots 8 and 9, Ligali Ayorinde Street, beside GAC Motors, Victoria Island, Lagos, from 9 am to 7 pm on both days. By combining premium fitness and recovery experiences with African music, culture, hospitality and specialist partnerships, BEYOND is demonstrating the potential for world-class wellness experiences created on the continent. As Williams puts it: “Africa has an incredible opportunity to shape the future of wellness. We have the creativity, talent, culture and a growing audience that understands the importance of investing in their wellbeing. Our ambition is to continue raising the standard of wellness experiences here while building a brand that helps people feel, function and live better.” As BEYOND on Tour enters its fifth edition, its message is simple: wellness is not only about how far we can push ourselves, but also about how intentionally we recover and care for ourselves along the way. It was a great opportunity to make new connections and discover more about the possibilities for destination celebrations across Africa. Then came lunch at Sunset Restaurant, overlooking Lake Victoria. I had a whole tilapia fish with sides, while some of my fellow delegates opted for chicken. With delicious food and that beautiful lake view, lunch was certainly a lovely way to spend the afternoon. Later that evening, we gathered for the Sound of Africa Dinner. Dressed in smart-casual white, delegates had another opportunity to mingle, enjoy the music and dance. You know we weren’t going to travel all the way to Uganda and spend every evening sitting quietly. Between the conversations, music and laughter, it was a lovely start to our ADCCE adventure. Day Two: Big Conversations About Africa’s Celebration Industry The second day brought us back to the conference venue for conversations about positioning Africa as a global destination for celebrations. ADCCE founder Jackline Nanteza shared how attending a similar event had inspired her to believe that African event planners could one day come together to showcase the continent to the world. The first panel explored selling Destination Africa to the global market and the challenges of attracting international events. Oruonye Kingsley Chimezie championed Africa as a destination for celebrations, while Farah Lodhi reminded attendees, “What I believe is that in events, nothing is impossible as long as you don’t give up.” Rahul Soman highlighted how photography and social media can bring Africa’s destinations closer to couples worldwide, while Carol Matibiri reflected on the influence of international destination marketing. The second panel, “Uganda’s Event-Ready Hospitality Ecosystem,” moderated by Kemi Omeke , brought together representatives from NIRA, Uganda Tourism Board, Entikko Safari Lodge and UACII, alongside Frank Murangwa and Amos Wekesa , to discuss the partnerships needed to support events in Uganda. We stayed at Entikko Safari Lodge, a beautiful retreat surrounded by nature. The food was another highlight, with so much to eat between our outings. Then came the safari the next morning. We spotted lions, giraffes, elephants, buffaloes and antelopes roaming the park. On our boat ride along the River Nile, we saw hippos and crocodiles in the water, offering us an even closer look at Uganda’s wildlife. Of course, we also visited Murchison Falls, often described as the world’s most powerful waterfall. Here, the River Nile squeezes through a gorge roughly seven metres wide before plunging about 43 metres. Seeing the rushing water and hearing its thunderous sound in person was an unforgettable experience. Between the wildlife, the breathtaking scenery and the delicious meals at Entikko, our Uganda adventure gave us plenty of memories to take home. One of my favourite parts of this trip was getting to experience Uganda with Oluwadunsin and Dorcas. Of course, we travelled for work, and ADCCE gave us the opportunity to meet professionals, learn about the destination celebrations industry and discover what different African businesses are creating. But there was also room to have fun together. We danced, laughed, explored new places, enjoyed the scenery and shared experiences that we’ll probably still be talking about long after returning home. And that’s one thing I appreciated about the structure of ADCCE 2026. The conference introduced us to the possibilities within Africa’s celebration and hospitality industries, while the familiarisation trip allowed us to see a destination beyond its meeting rooms and event venues. Uganda showed us its lakeside hospitality, its natural landscapes, its wildlife and some of the experiences that could make it an exciting choice for travellers and event organisers looking for something different. Until Next Time, Uganda! ADCCE 2026 brought together professionals with a shared interest in how Africa can welcome the world for celebrations, weddings, conferences and travel experiences. From the business conversations at Speke Resort Munyonyo to the adventures at Murchison Falls, the five-day experience gave us a lot to think about and even more to remember. We arrived in Uganda for a conference and left with new connections, fresh ideas, plenty of photographs and some wonderful travel memories. And if there’s one thing this trip has done, it’s given us even more reasons to explore Africa. item.title: Kikelomo Atanda-Owo Celebrates 20 Years in Media Unveils Podcast With Husband Reuben Abati
item.description: Ace broadcaster, media entrepreneur and host of Real Talk With Kike , Kikelomo Atanda-Owo , alongside her husband, veteran journalist and broadcaster Dr. Reuben Abati , has officially unveiled “ The Reuben and Kike Abati Podcast ,” marking an exciting new chapter in their broadcasting careers. The announcement was made on Saturday, October 10, 2026, during the celebration of Kikelomo Atanda-Owo’s 20 years in the media industry, held at Eko Hotels & Suites, Lagos. The occasion also commemorated the seventh anniversary of her flagship talk show, Real Talk With Kike, bringing together distinguished personalities, media executives, business leaders, industry stakeholders and well-wishers. The unveiling of The Reuben and Kike Abati Podcast represents a significant milestone for the celebrated media couple, who are bringing their wealth of experience, individual perspectives and shared passion for meaningful conversations to a new digital platform. The podcast is envisioned as a platform for engaging, thought-provoking and insightful conversations on issues shaping contemporary society, including governance, politics, relationships, family, culture, lifestyle, entertainment and everyday experiences. According to Lagos News Hub, combining Dr. Reuben Abati’s extensive background in journalism, political analysis and public affairs with Kikelomo Atanda-Owo’s distinctive approach to human-interest storytelling, lifestyle conversations and audience engagement, the podcast promises a compelling blend of perspectives, experience and authenticity. Beyond their individual accomplishments in broadcasting, the new podcast creates an opportunity for the couple to explore important subjects together, bringing their different professional experiences and viewpoints into conversations designed to inform, educate and entertain audiences. For Kikelomo Atanda-Owo, the unveiling comes at a particularly significant moment in her career as she celebrates two decades of consistency, resilience and impact in the Nigerian media landscape. Over the years, she has established herself as a respected voice in broadcasting, using Real Talk With Kike to facilitate conversations around personal development, relationships, social issues, leadership and the experiences that shape everyday life. Dr. Reuben Abati, on his part, brings decades of experience as a journalist, columnist, public affairs commentator and former presidential spokesperson. His contributions to political discourse and national conversations have established him as one of Nigeria’s recognisable media voices. Together, the couple will seek to create a distinctive podcast experience that combines serious conversations with relatable discussions, personal insights and engaging exchanges. item.description: Saskay celebrating her Master of Arts degree in Global Security and Strategy. Who says you need a suit to celebrate a master’s degree? Saskay is marking a major academic milestone on her own terms, swapping the Western-style outfit she originally planned for a look rooted in heritage. The Big Brother Naija star, whose real name is Tsakute Ladi Jonah , has earned a Master of Arts (MA) in Global Security and Strategy from VUB Brussels School of Governance, and her graduation photos make room for both her academic achievement and a conversation about how we dress for success. Reflecting on what the degree means to her, Saskay shared how studying a subject she has always been passionate about made the experience especially meaningful. Master of Arts (MA) in Global Security and Strategy. I got to study something I’ve always been passionate about, and that makes this degree mean so much more to me. I’ve poured so much of myself into this journey that my diploma is basically my baby. Saskay in the Hertunba Nola Kaftan for her graduation portraits. Her choice of outfit came about after her original plan fell through. Saskay had intended to wear a suit for the shoot, but her designer had an emergency and could not complete it in time. The change prompted her to reflect on why Western clothing is so often associated with academic achievement, and how graduation portraits can also celebrate cultural identity. I had a suit planned for this shoot, but my designer had an emergency and couldn’t get it ready in time. Things took a different turn, and it got me thinking about how we’ve come to associate education with western clothing. There’s something beautiful about celebrating an academic milestone in a way that also reflects who we are and where we come from. Saskay in her graduation outfit celebrating her MA in Global Security and Strategy. For the shoot, Saskay wore the Nola Kaftan by Hertunba, a flowing, 100% cotton design featuring motifs of palm trees, birds and dwellings. The motifs tell a metaphorical story of a small girl in a big village, with each illustration contributing to the larger narrative woven into the design. The kaftan featured a generous silhouette, fluid sleeves and an open drape, with its off-white and cream tones complemented by a chocolate brown silk veil. Saskay posing with her VUB Brussels School of Governance degree case. Oversized leaf-shaped gold drop earrings, a layered beaded gold necklace, thick gold cuffs, wide bangles and statement rings completed her look. item.title: Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle Becomes Nigeria’s Youngest Female Senior Advocate of Nigeria at 40
item.description: Judicial portrait of Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle SAN, partner at Afe Babalola & Co., who made history as Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria at the age of 40. Nigeria’s legal landscape has witnessed a momentous record as Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun – Adekunle joins the prestigious Inner Bar, officially becoming the youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) in history. Attaining the highly coveted Silk rank at the age of 40, the seasoned advocate and solicitor of the Supreme Court of Nigeria has broken a long-standing ceiling, setting a inspiring milestone for women across the legal profession and beyond. Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle, MCIArb, is a distinguished partner at the renowned law firm Afe Babalola & Co. (Emmanuel Chambers). With a career spanning over 14 years of legal practice, she specialises in complex litigation, commercial dispute resolution, strategic legal advisory, and international arbitration. Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle SAN following her elevation as the youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria. Her academic foundation includes a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) degree from Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, and a Master of Laws (LL.M.) in International Trade Law from the University of Leeds, United Kingdom. Before joining Afe Babalola & Co. as a Partner in September 2013, her professional experience included key positions at D. D. Dodo & Co. and the Nuhu Ribadu Campaign Organisation. Her historic elevation to Senior Advocate of Nigeria—a position reserved for legal practitioners who have distinguished themselves through exceptional skill, professional integrity, and significant contributions to Nigerian jurisprudence—marks a defining moment in contemporary law. Taking on the rank at 40 years old, she stands out as the youngest female lawyer to achieve this honour in Nigeria, carving a clear path for future generations of female lawyers to aim for the highest levels of leadership in the country’s judiciary and private bar. item.title: Before They Say “I Do”, See Zlatan Ibile & Davita Omoniyi’s Pre-Wedding Photos
item.description: Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi in an intimate pre-wedding portrait. Can you hear the wedding bells? Something beautiful is happening in Zlatan Ibile ’s world, and this time, it has nothing to do with a new song or music video. The Afrobeats star, whose real name is Omoniyi Temidayo Raphael , is getting ready to celebrate his love for longtime partner Davita Omoniyi in a grand wedding ceremony on 24 October 2026. And while we’re still waiting to see what the couple have planned for their big day, their pre-wedding photographs are already giving us plenty to admire. From the gorgeous colour choices to the fashion and the sweet way they pose together, Zlatan and Davita are making the countdown to their wedding even more exciting. The couple have been together for years and share two children. Davita, a UK-based media personality and entrepreneur, reportedly took on the Omoniyi surname following their private civil registry ceremony earlier this year. Now, with their wedding celebration approaching, they’re preparing to mark another chapter of their relationship surrounded by family and friends. Zlatan Ibile and Davita Omoniyi posing together in pastel outfits for their official pre-wedding pictures. For their pre-wedding photographs, celebrity stylist Emmanuel Goodnews Icon brought together a lovely combination of pastel ice blue and blush pink against a rich teal studio backdrop. The colours worked beautifully together, with Davita’s gown and Zlatan’s tailored outfit offering two different takes on the same colour palette. Davita wore a strapless mermaid gown by Lasosa By Pam Pam, featuring micro-pleating and ruching across the bodice. The fitted silhouette opened into a voluminous bubble-hem train made from bubblegum pink taffeta, giving the dress an interesting contrast of structure and volume. She completed her look with a high braided ponytail, glowing makeup, a classic tennis necklace and matching diamond jewellery. Davita Omoniyi in a custom gown by Lasosa By Pam Pam styled by Emmanuel Goodnews Icon. Beside her, Zlatan wore a bespoke light blue two-piece suit by T.I Nathan. His jacket featured a structured mandarin collar and concealed button placket, paired with relaxed wide-leg trousers. Dark wire-frame glasses and black patent leather shoes completed his look, keeping the styling simple while allowing the tailoring and colour to take centre stage. Zlatan Ibile styled by Emmanuel Goodnews Icon in a bespoke T.I Nathan suit The rich teal backdrop made the soft colours of their outfits even more striking, while their poses brought a lovely sense of closeness to the portraits. With 24 October just around the corner, the couple have given us a beautiful first look at their wedding style, and we’re curious to see what they’ll wear when the celebrations begin. item.title: An Icon Reimagined: Maltina Unveils New Look And Same Nourishing Taste
item.description: Maltina , Nigeria’s pioneering malt brand, has unveiled a new visual identity. The new look celebrates 50 years of nourishment while preserving the trusted taste Nigerians know and love. The new identity presents Maltina through a more contemporary lens across its glass bottles, cans and PET bottles. The brand’s signature orange has been strengthened, while enhanced gold elements create a more distinctive and premium presence on the shelf. New design cues, including the gold crown cork, brighter sunrays, a more prominent golden barley icon, a bolder calcium coin and the “Since 1976” heritage mark, bring Maltina’s story of nourishment and heritage to life. The look may be new, but the nourishing Maltina consumers know and trust remains unchanged. Maltina is fortified with calcium, with one 33cl bottle providing the equivalent of half a glass of milk. The brand is also endorsed by the Nutrition Society of Nigeria as a non-alcoholic drink rich in Vitamin A. “ For 50 years, Maltina has grown alongside generations of Nigerians. This refreshed identity is an evolution of a much-loved brand, designed to keep Maltina fresh, relevant and connected to today’s consumers while preserving the nourishing taste they know and trust, ” said Sarah Agha , Marketing Director, Nigerian Breweries Plc . Rather than define the new look for consumers, Maltina is inviting Nigerians to share their own first impressions through the “ What’s Your Word? ” campaign. Across media, retail and consumer experiences, people will be encouraged to look again and describe the refreshed identity in one word. “This relaunch is about more than a new pack. It is an invitation for Nigerians to help shape the next chapter of a brand that has been part of their lives for five decades. We look forward to hearing the words the new Maltina inspires,” Agha added. Consumers will encounter the refreshed packs in stores, restaurants, bars and markets, supported by a nationwide media rollout, trade launches and immersive consumer activations designed to help Nigerians discover and experience the new look. The invitation is simple: experience the new Maltina and tell us what you see. What’s Your Word for the New Maltina? https://maltina.nbplc.com/ . For 50 years, the brand has been part of Nigerian homes and everyday moments, bringing together nourishment, happiness and shared experiences across generations. item.title: Ayra Starr Is Taking Her Starrgirl World Tour to Europe and North America in 2027
item.description: Ayra Starr is set to bring her hit singles to the NFL London Game halftime show on 11th October Ladies and gentlemen, we reckon that cities in Europe, the UK and North America will come alive in purple from January 2027 to April 2027 because the Starrgirl herself, Ayra Starr , has officially announced her grand return to global stages. If you have been keeping up with global music headlines, you already know Oyinkansola Sarah Aderibigbe —famously known across the world as Ayra Starr—is in a league of her own. She recently made history as the very first African artiste to headline an NFL halftime show during the 2026 International Games fixture in London, treating a packed stadium crowd to a performance that cemented Afrobeats on one of sport’s biggest entertainment platforms. Fresh off that landmark milestone and the release of her third studio album, Starrgirl, the Mavin global sensation is packing her bags to take the project on a massive multi-continent run. Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London The upcoming Starrgirl World Tour kicks off its main international leg on 20 January 2027 in Cologne, Germany. From there, Ayra heads to Amsterdam on 21 January, Paris on 24 January, Milan on 27 January, Zurich on 29 January, and Brussels on 31 January. Her UK lovers get their turn on 2 February 2027, when she steps onto the London stage for a night that promises to be an absolute highlight of the winter season. North American fans pick up the excitement starting 18 March 2027 in Houston, Texas. The road trip continues across Dallas, Atlanta, Silver Spring, Boston, Philadelphia, Brooklyn, Chicago, Minneapolis, Denver, and San Francisco, alongside Canadian stops in Toronto and Montreal through early April. If you have been looking for the perfect excuse to hear catalogue favourites alongside fresh hits off her latest project like “ Gimme Dat ,” “ Tornado ,” “ Hot Body ,” and “ Heaven Baby ” live in an arena full of fans singing every word, this is your sign to pack your bags, align your travel dates, and experience the Starrgirl World Tour firsthand. Ayra Starr returns with her third studio album, Starrgirl. item.title: 5 New Music Videos You Need to Watch This Week: Victony, Tyla, Phyno & More
item.description: Nigerian singer-songwriter Victony wearing a glossy leather outfit on set during the production of the SLICK Remix, featuring American stars Don Toliver and Summer Walker, off his sophomore album STARLIFE. A new week calls for fresh music, and there’s plenty to add to your watchlist. From Victony bringing Don Toliver and Summer Walker into the mix for the “ SLICK ” remix to Tyla ’s dance-ready “ That Girl ” and Phyno ’s romantic “Beautiful”, there’s something for every mood. We’re also looking back at Ayra Starr ’s performance at the 2026 NFL international halftime show and making room for Anendlessocean ’s reflective “ Promises ”. Here are five music releases and performances to check out this week. Victony: “SLICK (Remix)” ft. Don Toliver & Summer Walker Victony has given “SLICK” a new twist, and this time, he’s brought Don Toliver and Summer Walker along for the ride. The original track appears on his sophomore album, STARLIFE, while the remix introduces a fresh mix of R&B vocals and melodies. With three artistes bringing their different sounds to the same record, there’s plenty to enjoy here. Tyla: “That Girl” If you’re looking for something to get you moving, Tyla has you covered with “That Girl” from her project A*Pop. The song draws on South Africa’s popular Phara Walk dance culture, pairing catchy rhythms with Tyla’s smooth vocals. It’s playful, danceable and one you might find yourself returning to throughout the week. Anendlessocean: “Promises” Anendlessocean offers a place for reflection, gratitude and rest with “Promises”. Rooted in faith and the assurance that God will come through again, the song invites listeners to pause, reflect and find comfort in the belief that He will do it again. It’s one to turn to when you need a little reminder to trust the journey. Phyno: “Beautiful” Ezege is back with “Beautiful”, a love letter to the woman who makes everything make sense. Smooth, heartfelt and unmistakably Phyno, the track blends Igbo, Pidgin and English over a melody made for the ones you hold close. Taken from his project Let That Sink In (LTSI), the song celebrates love in a way that feels personal and familiar. The official music video features actress and media personality Nancy Isime, giving the romantic track a visual companion. Ayra Starr: 2026 NFL Halftime Performance Ayra Starr took Afrobeats to the NFL international stage on 11 October, headlining the halftime show during the Philadelphia Eagles vs Jacksonville Jaguars game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. She opened her set with “Heaven Baby”, her collaboration with ZAYN, before performing “Santa”, “Rush” and “Dangerous”, and closing with a medley of “Hot Body” and “Ms. Paper”. The performance marked a major milestone for the Nigerian star, who became the first African artiste to headline an NFL International Games halftime show. item.title: Watch ‘Fishbone’, a 2020 Short Film by Anakle Films About Drug Counterfeiting
item.description: Years after its release, Fishbone remains relevant as Nigeria continues to grapple with counterfeit and substandard products. NAFDAC has repeatedly warned about falsified drugs and other products in circulation, including products that can lead to treatment failure, drug resistance and even death. Nigerians share their outcry on social media about their encounters with counterfeit products, from deodorant, chicken, toothpaste, to drinks, body and hair cream, soy sauce, palm oil, and many others. It is an ongoing public health concern. Released in 2020 by Anakle Films in collaboration with the US Mission in Nigeria and the US Department of Justice, Fishbone is a short film that explores the dangers of drug counterfeiting through the story of Mama T ( Shaffy Bello ), a respected philanthropist who secretly runs a counterfeit drug operation in Makoko, Lagos, and Inspector Cole ( Daniel Etim Effiong ), who is determined to bring her down. Beyond its crime-drama storyline, Fishbone explores the layers of counterfeiting, from the exploitation of vulnerable communities and the influence of wealth and social status to the devastating consequences of putting profit before human life. Its central message is particularly unsettling because the people who manufacture and distribute fake products can be deeply embedded in the same communities they endanger, without their knowledge. Rewatching Fishbone is an opportunity to remind ourselves how dangerous counterfeit products are. By showing how counterfeit drugs move through a community and affect people who may have no idea what they are buying, the film reminds viewers that awareness, vigilance and accountability matter. It is also a timely prompt to be more careful about where medicines are purchased and to report suspected falsified products to the appropriate authorities. Watch Fishbone again, and remember that behind every counterfeit product is a risk someone else may have to pay for with their life. item.description: From personalised skin consultations and hands-on product trials to picture-perfect Glow Cam portraits, Vaseline and Dove delivered a memorable experience at Beauty in the Motherland (BITML) 2026 . As sponsors, both brands made healthy skin the focus of the experience, inviting visitors to understand that “ The Real Flex Is Healthy Skin .” Held from 5–7 October at the Eko Convention Centre in Lagos, the event brought together Africa’s beauty professionals, brands, manufacturers, retailers, distributors, creators and consumers. Exhibitions and panel discussions explored everything from local manufacturing to skincare, haircare and the future of the continent’s beauty industry. Within that wider conversation, Vaseline and Dove encouraged beauty enthusiasts to move beyond simply following the latest skincare trend and spend time understanding their own skin. Their booth became a destination for visitors to get better acquainted with products they knew and discover others they could add to their routines. Vaseline’s and Dove’s pop-up booths stood out across the exhibition floor, drawing guests into an experience that encouraged them to ask, explore and try for themselves. At the Vaseline Skin Proof Lab and Texture Bar , guests explored textures, tried products, and spoke with Estheticians about their skin type. With Vaseline Original jellies, oils and lotions on deck, there was something for everyone and every skincare need. Dove extended that attention to underarm and body care through its Advanced Care range, exfoliating scrubs and Beauty Bar. Visitors explored the products and discussed how to give the skin beyond their face the same thoughtful attention. Event-exclusive discounts gave guests another reason to explore. Those who found a product they liked bought it at a discounted rate and received freebies, giving them more opportunities to add healthy skincare to their daily routine. But it was not all skincare. Adding excitement to the shopping and discovery experience, the Vaseline Glow Cam let guests strike a pose and smile for an instant Polaroid.
